text: The subject, Sana Tariq, a grocery wholesaler, received an unusually high volume of cash deposits at the Hyderabad Main Branch over a 26‑day period. Between 2026‑04‑02 and 2026‑04‑26 she deposited more than PKR 70 million in 26 separate cash‑deposit transactions, many exceeding PKR 2 million – the threshold that triggered CTR filings. Within the same month she executed three identical outbound IBFT payments of PKR 11,071,000 each (on 2026‑04‑05, 2026‑04‑12, 2026‑04‑19 and 2026‑04‑26) to the same counterparty, Metro FMCG Distributors, citing “STOCK INVOICE”. The pattern shows large cash inflows followed shortly by a single large electronic transfer that aggregates the cash, a classic “cash‑intensive business” structuring technique used to launder illicit funds. The subject’s declared monthly turnover (PKR 118 million) and income (PKR 1.4 million) are inconsistent with the volume of cash handled. No sanctions, PEP or adverse media matches were found, but the combination of high‑frequency, high‑value cash deposits, repeated identical large transfers to the same supplier, and the mismatch between declared income and transaction activity raises a strong suspicion of money‑laundering or illicit financing. An STR should therefore be filed.
